1.2.1.officialText: understand the terms function, domain, range, one-one function, inverse function and composition of functions

resources.title: Can we compose two simple functions?
resources.note: Canonical composition builder: fg vs gf order, powers f^i, all forms yielding 4x+4, f^i g f^j g^k.

resources.title: Can we draw the graph of  $\left| x + [x] \right|$?
resources.note: Range of |x+[x]|; one-one question; inverse of a restricted mapping. Floor function is an extension beyond P1 "simple cases".

resources.title: Can we find the ranges of $f$ and $g$, and the function $f \circ g$?
resources.note: Ranges of log_a x and 1/x; f∘g with h(x)+f(x)=0; why g∘f needs a restricted domain (the composite-formation condition); define both inverses fully. log/exp vocabulary sits in 9709 P2/P3 — the range/composition/inverse skills are exactly 1.2.x.

resources.title: Can we sketch the graph of $g \colon x \to x - [x]$?
resources.note: Ranges of [x] and x-[x]; sketch; solve f(x)=g(x) and fg(x)=gf(x). Floor function beyond P1 routine.

resources.title: Can we work with the domain, codomain and range of a bijection?
resources.note: Domain/codomain/range/bijective vocabulary; range of f and of g∘f; bijectivity <-> inverse existence. phi/psi cycle extends beyond P1 routine.

resources.title: Compose!
resources.note: Largest domain/range for A-D, then decompose composite functions — composition fluency package (pattern exemplar).

resources.title: Composing gets me nowhere
resources.note: ff(x)=x self-composition; self-inverse naming and examples — inverse fluency extension.

resources.title: Domain and range dominoes
resources.note: Describe domain/range in words then notation (domino fluency; pattern exemplar).

resources.title: Forming functions — defining domains
resources.note: Function = domain + rule + range; choose domains, state ranges, sketch; largest possible domain. Canonical 1.2.1 builder.

resources.title: Invertibles
resources.note: Match functions with their inverses (incl. domain-restricted quadratics <-> surds, fractional forms) and with graphs; draw inverse graphs. Card-sort pattern exemplar.

resources.title: Making inverse functions
resources.note: Function-machine inversion of f(x)=2x+1, then algebraic rearranging — scaffolded 1.2.3 intro (pattern exemplar).
